title: The Muziris Papyrus (SB XVIII 13167) — loan/cargo contract for the ship Hermapollon
language_note: Original Greek, Roman-Egyptian commercial/legal document. Held in the Papyrus Collection, Austrian National Library, Vienna (purchased 1980, first published 1985).
original_text_excerpt:
[recto, col. ii] δώσω καμηλείτηι ἀξιοχρέωι πρὸς ἐπίθεσιν τῆς εἰς Κόπτον
εἰσόδου καὶ ἀνοίσω διὰ τοῦ ὄρους μετὰ παραφυλακῆς καὶ ἀσφαλείας
εἰς τὰς ἐπὶ Κόπτου δημοσίας παραλημπτικὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ ποιήσω
ὑπὸ τὴν σὴν ἢ τῶν σῶν ἐπιτρόπων ἢ τοῦ παρόντος αὐτῶν
ἐξουσίαν καὶ σφραγεῖδα μέχρι ποταμοῦ ἐμβολῆς καὶ ἐμβαλοῦμαι
τῶι δέοντι καιρῶι εἰς ποταμὸν ἀσφαλὲς πλοῖον καὶ κατοίσω εἰς τὴν
ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ τῆς τετάρτης παραλημπτικὴν ἀποθήκην
καὶ ὁμοίως ποιήσω ὑπὸ τὴν σὴν ἢ τῶν σῶν ἐξουσίαν καὶ σφραγεῖδα. ταῖς
ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν μέχρι τεταρτολογίας δαπάναις πάσαις καὶ
φορέτρου ὄρους καὶ ναύλων ποταμίταις καὶ τῶν ἄλλων κατὰ μέρος
ἀναλωμάτων πρὸς τὸν ... ὄντων ... πρὸς τὸ ἐνστάντος τοῦ ἐν ταῖς
κατὰ Μουζεῖριν τοῦ δανείου συνγραφαῖς τῆς ἀποδόσεως ὡρισμένου
χρόνου ἐὰν μὴ δικαίως τότε χρεολυτῶ τὸ προκείμενον ἐν ἐμοὶ δάνειον

[verso, col. ii] νάρδου Γανγιτικῆς κιστῶν ξ ὧν ὁμοίως
τιμὴ λογίζεται ὡς τῆς κίστης (δραχμῶν) Δφ ἀργυρίου (τάλαντα) με
ἐλέφαντος ὑγιοῦς μὲν ὁλκ(ῆς) (τάλαντα) οη μν(ῶν) νδ
ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ τιμῆς μερῶν γ τῶν ἐκπεπλευκότων
ἐν τῷ Ἑρμαπόλλωνι πλοίῳ φορτίων ἀργυρίου (τάλαντα) Ανα (δραχμαὶ) Εωνβ
original_text_note: Verbatim Greek recovered 2026-08-09 from the DDbDP transcription of SB 18 13167 (Trismegistos 27666; ed. pr. Tyche 26 [2011] 199-233), served by papyri.info under CC BY 3.0. Two passages are excerpted: the recto transport clause (col. ii, lines 2-8) and the verso cargo valuation (col. ii, lines 1-4, 27-29). Editorial brackets marking lacunae, dots under uncertain letters, and line numbers have been removed for readability; column/line provenance is given inline. Consult papyri.info for the full critical apparatus. EXTENDED 2026-08-13: the recto excerpt ran to col. ii line 8 and therefore did not contain the port. **The record named Muziris in its title, its notes and the papyrus's conventional name, and nowhere in its own text** — the Vimose defect exactly, a claim carried by editorial scaffolding rather than by the source, and one that would have arrived downstream attached to a citation. Found while extracting subject places for A4. Now runs to col. ii line 14, which carries κατὰ Μουζεῖριν — 'the loan contracts made at Muziris' — so the Muziris-to-Alexandria route the record documents is attested by the record. Taken from the same DDbDP transcription already cited (papyri.info, CC BY 3.0), with the same normalisation as before. One departure, made explicit because the alternative is a silent join: at line 12 the DDbDP prints two lacunae of unstated length, and these are marked ' ... ' rather than closed up.
reference_translation: [Recto, loan/security contract clause] ...I will convey the goods through the desert under guard and protection up to the public tax-receiving warehouses at Koptos... [Verso, cargo valuation] Gangetic nard: 60 boxes, price reckoned at 4,500 drachmas of silver per box, 45 talents. Ivory: first grade, sound: 78 talents-weight 54¾ minas... Makes the price of the 3 parts of the cargoes shipped out in the ship 'Hermapollon' 1,154 talents 2,852 drachmas of silver.
translation_source: D. Rathbone, 'The Muziris papyrus (SB XVIII.13167): financing Roman trade with India', Bulletin of the American Society of Papyrologists 46 (2000), pp. 39-50, as hosted on Attalus.org (Select Papyri 1.187A).
notes: Direct documentary evidence of the financial scale of Rome-India trade: this single cargo (nard, ivory, and other goods, ivory/nard portion alone valued near 1,154 talents of silver) corroborates the 'gold for pepper' exchange described in Akananuru 149 (southasia-01) and the Periplus (southasia-02) with hard numbers. High-value hero-demo candidate for showing how a legal/financial document, a poem, and a geography text all converge on the same trade relationship.

subject_places.name: Muziris
subject_places.note: κατὰ Μουζεῖριν at recto col. ii line 12 — 'the loan contracts made at Muziris'. **This record did not name its own port until 2026-08-13**: the excerpt ran to line 8, and Muziris appeared only in the title, the notes and the papyrus's conventional name. 50146 Muziris 10.154/76.213, 'settlement, port', -30..640, locationPrecision 'precise'. That coordinate IS Pattanam. Pleiades has therefore already adopted the identification `southasia-04-pattanam` treats as open, and marks it precise; read that record's findspot note before changing this one. What is contested there is whether the excavation site is Muziris — a claim about the coordinate. What this record does is name the place, which is why the ground here is 'stated' and the contested flag is not repeated: per PLACES.md, contested belongs to an identification, not to the fact that a text names a place.

subject_places.name: Koptos
subject_places.note: Κόπτος, twice in the recto — the goods go by camel across the desert to the public tax-receiving warehouses there, then down the river. 786010 Coptos 25.996/32.816, 'settlement, port, archaeological-site', -750..640 — modern Qift on the Nile.

subject_places.name: Alexandria
subject_places.note: εἰς τὴν ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ τῆς τετάρτης παραλημπτικὴν ἀποθήκην — the warehouse of the fourth-tax at Alexandria, where the cargo ends. 727070 Alexandria 31.201/29.910, 'settlement, port', -2010..2000. Refused: the forty-odd other Alexandrias, in Aria, Carmania, Arachosia and elsewhere, which a title search returns first.

subject_places.name: the Ganges
subject_places.note: νάρδου Γανγιτικῆς on the verso — Gangetic nard, sixty boxes of it, the first item of the cargo valuation. Named adjectivally, which is how the text attests it. Same id and the same refusal as `southasia-02`: 49984 is a river in Sri Lanka.
